editorial:
Imagine sending a video message directly to the president of the EU Commission to tell him how to run things. That is exactly what happens here. You get a weird and wild mix of styles that feels more like a creative project than a standard drama. It is only five minutes long, but it packs a punch by switching between real-life footage and cool animation. The vibe is a bit like a high-energy presentation designed to wake someone up and make them think about how alcohol laws work in Europe, specifically focusing on why the Swedish system is a good idea.

What really stands out is how the director keeps things moving fast. You will not get bored because the visuals change every few seconds. The biggest pro is the creativity, though the con is that it is very short, so you might want more. If you enjoy short films that have a strong message, you should definitely check this out. Since it was made for the web, you can find it online easily, but if you can find a high-quality 4K version to stream or add to your digital collection, it makes those animated segments look even sharper.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by making a final, strong plea to Mr. Barroso. It stops jumping between styles and delivers a clear message about public health. The end basically tells the EU leader that the Swedish monopoly on alcohol sales helps keep people safe and healthy. There is no big plot twist since it is a political message, but it ends on a serious note, hoping the president will actually listen to the advice provided.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves short films with a social message.
